transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I came in because my mind just doesn’t seem to hold onto things the way it used to. That’s the part that’s really been frightening me. I’ll sit down to do something simple, like write a little note for the youth maker program—something I’ve done so many times I shouldn’t even have to think about it—and suddenly the words and numbers just scatter. I look at the page and it’s like I can’t keep the thread in my head long enough to get it down.

I used to be able to do that sort of thing almost automatically, you know? Just make a list, jot down measurements or times or names, put a note together. Now I’ll start, stop, reread the same line, lose what I meant to say, and then I’m just sitting there with the pen in my hand feeling… I don’t know, stuck. That’s why I’m here.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, not voices like someone talking to me when nobody’s there. I haven’t had that, at least not that I’ve noticed.

Sometimes I’ll sort of think I hear the house settling, or a noise outside, and I’ll stop and listen because I’m already on edge about myself lately… but that’s not the same as voices. Nobody’s calling my name or telling me things or anything like that.
Have you been feeling depressed lately?

Yes… yes, I have. Most days, honestly. It’s not just feeling a little down or having a bad morning. I wake up and there’s this heavy, hollow feeling right here in my chest, like it’s already waiting for me before I’ve even opened my eyes properly.

And even when my wife is being kind to me — and she is, she really tries — I still feel… far away from it somehow. Like I can hear her being gentle, I can understand that she cares, but it doesn’t reach me the way it should. It’s like I’m sitting at the bottom of a well, looking up at everything and everyone, and they’re all somewhere above me. I know they’re there, but I can’t quite get to them.
Because of these memory and concentration problems, do you need help managing your usual day-to-day tasks?

Yes… I do. More than I want to admit, really. It’s not just that I misplace something or forget a name now and then. I’ve let whole parts of my life slip out of my hands.

I used to handle things at church without thinking much of it — little responsibilities, helping where I said I’d help, keeping track of what needed doing. And the garden too… that was always mine, something steady. I knew what needed watering, what needed pruning, what was coming up next. Now I’ll look out at it and feel like I can’t even begin, like there are too many steps between me and just walking outside.

And the youth maker program… that one hurts. I used to feel useful there. I could be in the workshop, help the kids with measurements, tools, keeping things organized and safe. But lately I don’t feel safe being by myself in there. I don’t trust my concentration enough. I’ll lose track of what I’m doing, or I’ll stand there unsure of the next step, and with tools around… I just don’t feel right about it.

So my wife has had to step in more than she should, and my pastor too. They’ve picked up things I used to manage. I’m grateful, but it’s embarrassing. It makes me feel like I’m disappearing from my own life, piece by piece.
Do you feel that you’ve done something terribly wrong or that you’re to blame for bad things happening?

I… I don’t know that I’d say I’ve done something terribly wrong, exactly. Not in the sense of some big unforgivable thing, if that’s what you mean.

But I do spend a lot of time thinking I’ve let people down. My wife, especially. And people who counted on me. I keep going over things I should have done better, or kept up with, or noticed sooner. Sometimes it feels like if I had just been stronger or more organized or less… whatever this is… then other people wouldn’t have to carry so much.

So no, I don’t think I’m responsible for bad things happening in the world or anything like that. But I do feel guilty. A lot. It’s hard to separate what’s reasonable from what’s just me turning everything back on myself.
Did your memory and concentration problems start before you began feeling depressed?

I think… no, I don’t think they really started before. At least not in any way I noticed.

What brought me in — what really scared me — was that my mind just stopped holding onto things the way it used to. I’d sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program, something I used to be able to do almost without thinking, and suddenly the numbers and words would just… scatter on me. I’d look at the page and know there was something I meant to put down, but it wouldn’t stay in order long enough to write it.

And that seemed to come along with this low feeling, or maybe after it had already settled in. It’s hard to untangle exactly, because once you’re in it, the days blur together. But I wouldn’t say I had clear memory and concentration problems first and then got depressed afterward. It feels more like my thinking got foggy as everything else got heavier.
Do you believe you deserve to be punished for what is happening?

Punished… I don’t know. I don’t think I’d put it that way.

I mean, I feel ashamed, and I feel like I’ve failed in ways I can’t quite fix, but “deserve to be punished” sounds… harsher than what I tell myself, I think. I’m not sitting there thinking someone should punish me, or that I need to suffer to make things right.

But I do get into this place where I feel like maybe I don’t deserve much kindness either. Like if people are frustrated with me, part of me thinks, well, maybe that’s fair. Maybe I’ve earned that. So I’m not sure how to answer cleanly. I don’t believe I deserve some punishment, exactly… but I do carry this feeling that I’ve brought a lot of it on myself somehow.
Have you been feeling as if parts of your body, or even you yourself, are dead or no longer really existing?

No… no, I don’t think so. Not like parts of me are dead, or that I’m not really existing.

I do sometimes feel sort of distant from myself, if that makes sense — like I’m moving through things without much feeling — but I wouldn’t say I believe my body is dead or missing or anything like that. I still feel… here. Maybe not very present or lively, but here.

When you ask it that way, it sounds more like something very specific, and I don’t think I’ve had that. I haven’t been sitting there thinking, “My arm is dead,” or “I don’t exist.” It’s more just… emptiness, I guess, but not that I’m literally gone.
Have you had any fixed beliefs that something is seriously wrong with your body or that your organs are failing, even when others tell you that isn’t true?

No… I don’t think I’ve had that kind of belief.

I mean, I worry about myself, of course, and when you feel awful for long enough it’s easy to start wondering if something is just deeply wrong with you. But I haven’t been convinced that my organs are failing or that there’s some serious physical catastrophe happening that nobody else can see.

If someone told me, “Your heart is fine,” or “Your stomach isn’t shutting down,” I don’t think I’d be arguing with them or secretly believing they were wrong. It’s more… I feel worn down, but not in that specific way where I’m sure my body is broken despite what people say.
Have your memory and thinking problems been steadily getting worse over time?

Yes… yes, that’s actually one of the main reasons I came in.

It feels like my mind just won’t hold onto things anymore. I’ll sit down to write something simple, like a note for the youth maker program — something I used to be able to do almost without thinking — and suddenly the words don’t stay where they’re supposed to. The numbers get away from me, the order of things slips, and I’m staring at the page like I’ve forgotten how to do a very ordinary task.

And it’s not just frustrating, it’s frightening, because I know what I used to be able to do. I’ll start with a clear thought, or at least I think it’s clear, and then halfway through it scatters. I have to keep going back, rereading, trying to remember what I meant to say. So yes, it does feel like it’s been getting worse over time, or at least more noticeable and harder to work around.
On days when your mood is a little better, do the memory and concentration problems still feel just as bad?

Yes… even on the days when I feel a little more like myself, the thinking problem is still there. Maybe I’m less overwhelmed by it on those days, but it doesn’t just clear up.

That’s actually part of why it scares me. I came in because my mind just will not hold onto things anymore. I’ll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program — something I used to be able to do practically in my sleep — and then the numbers and the words just scatter on me. I’ll know what I meant to say, or I’ll think I know, and then when I try to put it down it’s like the order disappears.

On a slightly better day, I might not get as upset immediately, but I still have to reread things over and over, and I still lose the thread. It’s not like, “Oh, my mood lifted a bit and now I can think clearly again.” I wish it were that simple. The concentration and memory problems still feel pretty bad.
Has there been a clear decline in your memory or thinking compared with how you used to be?

Yes. There has. That’s the part that bothers me so much, because I can feel the difference between how I used to be and how I am now.

I used to be able to sit down and write out a simple note for the youth maker program almost automatically. I mean, it wasn’t some complicated thing — just a few sentences, maybe some numbers or dates or instructions — and I could keep it all straight in my head while I was doing it. Now I sit there, and it’s like my mind just will not hold onto the pieces long enough. The words scatter, the numbers don’t stay in order, and I lose what I was trying to say halfway through.

It’s not just that I’m a little slower. It feels like a real drop from what was normal for me. I’ll look at the page and think, “Why is this so hard now?” because this was something I could’ve done in my sleep before.
Have you ever gotten lost in a place that should have been familiar to you?

I don’t know that I’d say I’ve gotten lost somewhere familiar, not exactly. That hasn’t been the main thing I’ve noticed.

What’s been happening is more like… my mind won’t keep hold of ordinary things the way it used to. Like I’ll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program — something I honestly could have done in my sleep before — and suddenly the numbers and the words just scatter on me. I can’t keep them in order, and I lose the thread of what I was trying to say.

So it’s not so much that I’m wandering around confused about where I am. It’s more that when I try to do something simple and familiar, my thinking doesn’t stay together. That’s what’s been scaring me.
Because of your memory or thinking problems, have you needed someone else to take over paying bills or managing your medicines?

I haven’t had someone take over bills or medicines in that kind of formal way… not that exactly. It’s more that I’ve started to feel like I can’t trust my mind with simple things the way I used to.

What brought me in is that my mind just will not hold onto things anymore. Like, I’ll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program — something I honestly used to be able to do in my sleep — and then the numbers and words just scatter on me. I’ll have the sentence, or the date, or whatever small detail in my head, and then when I try to put it down, it’s gone or jumbled. I end up staring at it, rereading it, trying to reconstruct what I meant.

So, no, I don’t think anyone has fully taken over bills or medications because of it. But the same problem that would make that hard is definitely there — I just can’t keep things organized in my head the way I used to, and it scares me.
Have you had any memory or thinking tests done by a doctor that showed a problem?

I don’t think so… not in any formal way that I remember. I mean, nobody has sat me down and said, “Here are the results, and this shows a definite problem,” if that’s what you mean.

I’ve answered questions at appointments, and people ask me about how I’m doing, but I’m not sure if that counts as a memory test. I don’t want to say yes if it wasn’t really one. As far as I know, I haven’t had one of those official thinking or memory tests that came back showing something.
Have any of your doctors told you that a medical condition affecting your brain is causing these memory and thinking problems?

No… I don’t think anyone has told me that, not in those words. No doctor has said, “You have this brain condition and that’s why your memory or thinking is off,” or anything that definite.

I’ve worried about it, of course, because when your mind starts feeling unreliable, you start wondering what it means. But as far as what I’ve actually been told by doctors, I don’t have some clear explanation like that. If someone mentioned a possibility in passing, I may not be remembering it perfectly, but I don’t believe anyone has diagnosed me with a medical brain condition causing it.
Because of your memory or thinking problems, have you gotten lost while driving or been unable to find your way on a familiar route?

I don’t think it’s shown up that way, exactly — not like I’ve gotten lost driving on a route I know. It’s more… the problem is in my head holding onto things.

What made me come in is that I’ll sit down to do something simple, like write a short note for the youth maker program, something I used to do without even thinking about it, and suddenly the numbers or the words just won’t stay put. They scatter on me. I’ll know what I meant to write, and then a second later it’s jumbled or gone, and I’m sitting there trying to piece it back together.

So with familiar routes, no, I can’t say I’ve been unable to find my way. But that same feeling — like my mind isn’t reliable the way it used to be — that’s what’s been scaring me.
Because of your memory or thinking problems, have you needed someone else to manage your finances for you?

I haven’t had someone take over my finances for me, no… not formally like that. I still try to handle things myself. But I’ll be honest, it frightens me more than it used to, because the problem feels like my mind just will not hold onto things anymore.

It’s the same kind of thing I mentioned — I sit down to write something simple, like a short note for the youth maker program, something I used to be able to do almost in my sleep, and the numbers and words just scatter on me. I’ll look at them and think, “Wait, what was I doing?” or I’ll have the thought there and then it slips before I can get it down properly.

So with bills or money, I’m not saying someone else has had to manage it for me, but the reason I’m here is that this kind of slipping, this inability to keep the words or numbers steady in my head, has gotten scary.
Has your wife noticed that your memory or thinking has clearly gotten worse?

My wife… yes, I think she has noticed, though I don’t know if she would put it exactly that way, like “clearly worse.” But she sees me get stuck. She sees that I can’t seem to keep things in my head the way I used to.

The thing that really made me come in is that my mind just will not hold onto things anymore. I’ll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program — something I could’ve done in my sleep before, honestly — and the numbers and words just scatter on me. I’ll have the sentence or the thought, and then it breaks apart before I can get it down. And I’ll sit there staring at it, trying to gather it back up.

So yes, I’m pretty sure she’s noticed something is different, because it’s not subtle to me anymore. It’s frightening.
Has a doctor ever told you that you scored poorly on a formal memory or thinking test?

No, I don’t think a doctor has told me that, not in those words. I haven’t had someone sit me down and say, “You scored poorly on this formal memory test,” or anything like that.

What I can tell you is why I came in, which is… my mind just will not hold onto things anymore. I’ll sit down to write something simple, like a note for the youth maker program — something I used to be able to do almost without thinking — and the numbers and words just scatter on me. I can see what I’m trying to say, or I think I can, and then it sort of breaks apart before I can get it onto the page. It’s hard to explain without sounding dramatic, but it feels like I’m trying to hold water in my hands.

So, no formal poor score that I know of. It’s more that in real life, doing simple things I used to do easily, I can feel something isn’t working right.

patient.answer:
Punished… I don’t know. I don’t think I’d put it that way.

I mean, I feel ashamed, and I feel like I’ve failed in ways I can’t quite fix, but “deserve to be punished” sounds… harsher than what I tell myself, I think. I’m not sitting there thinking someone should punish me, or that I need to suffer to make things right.

But I do get into this place where I feel like maybe I don’t deserve much kindness either. Like if people are frustrated with me, part of me thinks, well, maybe that’s fair. Maybe I’ve earned that. So I’m not sure how to answer cleanly. I don’t believe I deserve some punishment, exactly… but I do carry this feeling that I’ve brought a lot of it on myself somehow.
